# Results — Study 202 (Fifty-Two-Week-Low) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Signal: 52-week-low
proximity = (close − 252d low) / (252d high − 252d low).  Stocks ranked cross-sectionally
by proximity; Q1 = nearest 52-week low (the contrarian long), Q5 = nearest 52-week high.
Equal-weight quintile portfolios, forward log-return measured at 5, 20, and 65 trading days.
Rebalanced every 5 trading days.  Universe: 20 representative S&P 500 large-cap names
(AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META, NVDA, JPM, JNJ, XOM, PG, V, MA, HD, UNH, CVX, MRK, ABBV,
PEP, KO, WMT).  **Survivorship-biased** — all names still trade as of 2026-06-15.
As-of **2026-06-15**.  Panel: 3,383 days × 20 tickers, 2013-01-02 → 2026-06-15.*

## The honest test — Q1-minus-Q5 spread (gross, cost = 0)

Stocks sorted by proximity to 52-week low (ascending), equal-weight quintile
portfolios, forward return over 5 trading days, rebalanced weekly (n = 626 periods).

| Quintile | label | mean return (bps/period) | HAC *t* | ann. return (%) |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **Q1** | near 52-week low | **+25.80** | +2.39 | **+9.3%** |
| Q2 | low-intermediate | +26.73 | +2.62 | +9.7% |
| Q3 | middle | +27.57 | +2.81 | +10.0% |
| Q4 | high-intermediate | +30.78 | +3.56 | +11.2% |
| **Q5** | near 52-week high | **+33.22** | +3.71 | **+12.0%** |
| **Q1 − Q5 spread** | contrarian long-short | **−7.42** | **−0.67** | — |

**Key finding:** Q5 (near the 52-week high) *outperforms* Q1 (near the 52-week low)
across all tested horizons. The Q1-Q5 spread is **negative** — the contrarian thesis
is wrong in direction — and statistically insignificant (HAC *t* = −0.67).

Far from bouncing back, stocks near their 52-week low *continue to lag*.
This is a mild momentum result, not a contrarian one.

## Hold-period sweep (Q1-Q5 spread, gross)

| Hold period | spread (bps/period) | HAC *t* | n periods |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day | **−11.12** | **−2.00** | 627 |
| 5 days | −7.42 | −0.67 | 626 |
| 10 days | −7.63 | −0.36 | 625 |
| 20 days | −8.13 | −0.21 | 623 |
| 65 days | −37.30 | −0.45 | 614 |

The 1-day hold is the only period with |*t*| ≥ 2, and it is in the **wrong direction**
for the contrarian story (spread = −11 bps, *t* = −2.00): stocks near their 52-week
low *underperform* stocks near their high over the next single trading day.
This is consistent with short-term price momentum, not mean-reversion.

## Long-only comparison: bottom decile vs equal-weight baseline (5-day hold)

| Arm | mean (bps/period) | ann. return | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Bottom decile (near 52w-low) | +23.60 | +8.5%/yr | +1.62 |
| Equal-weight basket (baseline) | +31.51 | +11.3%/yr | +4.26 |
| Spread (bottom − baseline) | **−7.92** | — | **−0.72** |

A long-only investor buying the 10% of names closest to their 52-week lows would
have earned **+8.5%/yr** against a **+11.3%/yr** equal-weight baseline — a drag of
almost 3 percentage points per year, with no statistical significance to hang a thesis on.

## Survivorship bias note

The universe is locked to 20 names that are all current S&P 500 constituents and
still trade in 2026.  This *inflates* all quintile returns (failed companies, which
hit 52-week lows and kept falling, are excluded).  The **bias works against** the
contrarian story: even with the deck stacked in its favour (no bankruptcies, no
delisted losers), the 52-week-low quintile still underperforms the high-proximity
quintile.  On an unbiased universe the result would likely be even more negative.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine knows the difference

On a deterministic synthetic panel, the Q1-Q5 spread is monotone in the planted
AR(1) reversion coefficient, confirming the engine is a faithful detector:

| Planted AR(1) | description | spread (bps) | HAC *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| −0.40 | strong momentum | −77 | −4.4 |
| 0.00 | martingale | −8 | −0.7 |
| +0.40 | strong reversion | +16 | +1.8 |

The real tape sits firmly in the "mild momentum / martingale" regime.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Q1-Q5 spread = −7.42 bps/period, HAC *t* = −0.67;
  statistically indistinguishable from zero and *in the wrong direction* for the
  contrarian thesis.  At the 1-day horizon the spread is significant (*t* = −2.00)
  but also in the wrong direction — consistent with momentum, not contrarianism.
  Survivorship bias is named: the real-world result on an unbiased universe
  is likely more negative.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The strategy underperforms a passive equal-weight
  baseline before any costs.  Adding realistic transaction costs, wider bid-ask
  spreads on beaten-down names, and market-impact from herding into illiquid
  losers would make it an outright loser.
